system.name: DARTH-PUM
system.one_liner: a general-purpose hybrid processing-using-memory (PUM) architecture that tightly integrates analog and digital PUM within each compute tile

components.name: Front End
components.role: fetches and decodes hybrid PUM instructions and issues PUM-specific micro-ops (Fetch, Decode, Issue)

components.name: Hybrid Compute Tile
components.role: replicated back-end tile that executes hybrid PUM kernels; multiple tiles form the back end

components.name: Analog Compute Element
components.role: performs analog MVM operations, coordinated by an A/D arbiter, transpose unit, and instruction injection unit

components.name: A/D Arbiter
components.role: sequences operations and data movement between the analog and digital compute elements

components.name: Transpose Unit
components.role: supports data transposition between analog and digital domains

components.name: Instruction Injection Unit
components.role: per-HCT unit that reduces micro-op expansion overhead and mitigates front-end stalls

components.name: Digital Compute Element
components.role: performs digital PUM (non-MVM) operations dispatched from digital issue queues

components.name: Digital PUM µop Queues
components.role: digital issue queue dispatching micro-ops to the digital PUM arrays

flows.what: 8B/cycle I/O data transfer, rate-matching ADC throughput with DCE write bandwidth

content.key_idea: DARTH-PUM pairs a shared front-end controller with a grid of Hybrid Compute Tiles, each tile fusing an Analog Compute Element and a Digital Compute Element through an arbitrated, rate-matched interface so analog MVM and digital non-MVM operations execute together in memory.
content.reading_order: Left grid of repeated Hybrid Compute Tiles around a central Front End box, with a callout zooming into one tile to show the stacked Analog Compute Element above the Digital Compute Element.

evidence: DARTH-PUM consists of two parts, as shown in Figure 8: (1) a front-end controller ... and (2) a back end composed of multiple hybrid compute tiles
We connect the ACE and DCE using an I/O data transfer network capable of transferring 8 B per cycle
we introduce an analog–digital arbiter and an instruction injection unit to sequence operations and data movement

summary: This figure shows the DARTH-PUM hardware architecture. A shared Front End (Fetch, Decode, Issue) sits amid a grid of replicated Hybrid Compute Tiles (HCTs) that form the back end. A callout zooms into one HCT to reveal its internal structure: an Analog Compute Element (with an A/D arbiter, a transpose unit, and an instruction injection unit driving analog PUM arrays) stacked above a Digital Compute Element (with digital PUM micro-op queues driving digital PUM arrays). The two compute elements are connected by an 8-byte-per-cycle I/O data transfer network that rate-matches ADC throughput to digital-array write bandwidth, letting analog MVM and digital non-MVM operations cooperate within the same tile. The figure combines a tile-array diagram with a magnified internal block diagram, using purple for tile/front-end structures and green/yellow versus blue/navy to separate the analog and digital compute elements.
